title: Communication Is Everything. Everything Is Communication.
author: Chris O'Brien
summary: Chris O'Brien (adapted from 'The Systemic Principal') opens with a Thursday parent conference scenario -- five teachers leave early or stay late based on different hallway answers, a family arrives for a missed appointment -- to show what a broken communication system looks like. The problem is not that nobody communicated; it is a design problem. When a school has no designed Communication System, the principal becomes one by default, creating unequal information environments where those with proximity to the principal know what is happening and everyone else fills the gap with rumor, assumption, and fear. The solution is a four-subsystem Communication System: (1) Weekly Rhythm -- Wednesday leadership team meeting where decisions are made and action steps are owned, plus Friday staff email where the week becomes legible to everyone at the same time; (2) Communication Cascade -- information reaches leaders before staff and staff before families, so leaders can be stewards of the message; (3) Principal's Voice -- communication only the principal can make (vision, hard truths, change announcements), protected by restraint; (4) Feedback Architecture -- designed upward channels including the 24/48 rule (if still bothering you 24 hours later, address it directly within 48, then let it go). Together, the four subsystems produce a school where the principal stops being the communication system and becomes the leader of one.
points: * When a school has no designed Communication System, the principal becomes one by default -- creating an information environment where proximity to the principal determines what staff know, and the gap fills with rumor and fear. * The Weekly Rhythm (Wednesday leadership meeting + Friday staff email) ensures the hallway question never has to happen: the answer was already in the email, the decision was already in the meeting. * The Communication Cascade -- leaders briefed before staff, staff before families -- protects leaders' ability to steward the message rather than receive it alongside their teams. * The Principal's Voice is what only the principal can say: vision, hard truths, change announced in language that holds. It loses weight when deployed too often; restraint is the design choice that protects it. * Feedback Architecture designs upward channels rather than leaving them informal -- the 24/48 rule: if still bothering you 24 hours later, address directly with that person within 48 hours; after that, let it go.
quotes: This is what a broken Communication System looks like. Not because nobody communicated. Because the principal was the communication system.
When a school has no designed Communication System, the principal becomes one -- by default, by necessity, by the absence of an alternative.
a well-designed school communication culture is the residue of intentionally designed repetition.
Restraint is a design choice. Voice is what you protect for the moments that require it.
A leader who cannot receive feedback cannot credibly give it.
A staff that has no designed upward channel will build informal ones -- and those informal channels rarely reach the principal until the damage is already done.
The principal who designs this system stops being the communication system. They become the leader of one. That is a different job. It is also, finally, a sustainable one.
